transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Support), Maya Chen (Quantaco Head of MLOps), Arjun Patel (Quantaco SRE), Sofia Ruiz (Quantaco Eng Manager), Leo Tan (Quantaco ML Eng)

Summary: quick review of the POC cost/unit economics, looked at tokens/sec per dollar metrics across hosted vs dedicated, examined caching hit rates and estimated savings, discussed batching tradeoffs and tail latency. Agreed to run two more batch-size benchmarks and to finalize cost spreadsheet with assumptions.

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — is this still a good time?
[00:10] Maya: yep all good, thanks.
[00:18] Diego: cool, I'll jump into the cost numbers we ran this week. quick context: these runs are on the rwd-v2-curie-ish model variant, quantized to q4_0 in the dedicated pool, and the workload is our sample customer traffic with a 35% prefix reuse.
[00:33] Diego: baseline hosted runs (no cache, bs=1) gave us ~28 tokens/sec per dollar on average, with obvious p95 latency 320ms for short seqs. when we enabled prefix/KV cache with the same model we saw effective tokens/sec per dollar jump to ~96. so that's about a 3.4x improvement in token economics just from caching. note: those numbers are approximate, see spreadsheet.
[01:05] Arjun: wait the 96 number is tokens per dollar or tokens per second?
[01:08] Diego: tokens per dollar. so more tokens processed for the same spend; throughput (tokens/sec) also improved because cache avoids recomputation on prefix.
[01:18] Leo: curious about the cache hit rate you observed — what's the hit %?
[01:21] Diego: we measured a 58% hit rate on the prefix set for the sample workload. with a heavier prefix reuse like 70% it jumps to about 120 tokens/sec per dollar equivalent. i want to caveat that our instrumentation sometimes labels hits as micro-hits when only KV partial matches, so there's a slight over-estimate margin.
[01:45] Sofia: and for batching — we saw tradeoffs right? bigger batch sizes help cost but hurt latency. can you quantify?
[01:50] Diego: yes. bs=1 median latency around 210ms, bs=8 median 350ms but throughput increases ~2.6x. bs=16 median 520ms, throughput up about 3.6x but p95 starts to spike. so it's a classic cost vs latency tradeoff. for their P95 SLO of ~450ms, bs=8 is feasible; bs=16 may cause SLO violations at peak.
[02:20] Maya: our app cares more about median and p95 for interactive sessions — we can't sacrifice p95 above 450ms. so 8 seems promising.
[02:30] Lena: one lever we recommend is dynamic batching policy — enable batching up to 8 for interactive routes and allow larger batch sizes for background or async routes. also combine with prefix caching to reduce latency impact.
[02:45] Diego: also quantization profile — q4_0 is good; moving to q3 or q2 (if available) could give an extra ~20-40% cost reduction but might degrade quality on some prompts. we didn't run exhaustive evals yet.
[02:58] Arjun: are there memory or KV cache size implications for higher cache rates? how much RAM did you allocate?
[03:04] Diego: the dedicated node we used had 384GB GPU RAM equivalent (approx), we kept kv cache at default 32GB for this run. bumping KV to 64GB increases hit rate in long-tail but has diminishing returns beyond ~70% reuse for this dataset.
[03:25] Leo: can you share the logs that show token counts and billing matches?
[03:28] Diego: yes — will attach the benchmark logs and the per-run CSV in the shared folder. Lena will put the cost model link in the follow-up.
[03:35] Samir: small note — our billing calc uses per-token billing plus small infra surcharge; we normalize to dollars by dividing tokens processed by tokens-per-dollar metric derived from infra cost. slight rounding differences possible.
[03:50] Maya: can we see an example scenario when caching is low — like 10-20% reuse — what does cost look like?
[03:55] Diego: good question — with only 20% cache hit, tokens/sec per dollar drops to ~40 for bs=1; with bs=8 and 20% cache we get ~95 tokens per dollar. so batching helps but caching is the biggest lever for interactive workloads.
[04:15] Sofia: are there any differences between hosted and dedicated when it comes to cache sharing across customers? we want isolated data.
[04:22] Lena: by default cache is per-customer in Dedicated and Private — we never share across tenants. hosted may use shared infrastructure but we maintain logical isolation; for regulatory needs we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:35] Maya: competitor question — LargeCloudAI advertises pre-warmed hosts which help latency; how does Redwood compare?
[04:41] Diego: we're similar in warm-start strategies but Redwood has more aggressive KV prefix caching and auto-batching heuristics tuned for LLM workloads; our numbers here reflect that. also routing fallback and model variants can reduce tail cost in pressure events.
[04:58] Arjun: what about cold-starts? if traffic spikes from zero how is tokens/sec per dollar impacted?
[05:03] Diego: cold starts can double latency for first few requests; we recommend a small pre-warm pool or keepalive pings during release windows. economically, cold starts are small fraction of tokens but matter for latency SLOs.
[05:20] Lena: quick recap of the cost spreadsheet assumptions: model variant q4_0, base infra cost X (linked in sheet), cache default 32GB, batch policy tested at 1/8/16, measurement window 30 minutes simulated traffic at 50 qps.
[05:36] Maya: are you comfortable publishing the raw benchmark CSVs? we want to run same locally.
[05:40] Diego: yes, we'll share CSVs and the small runner script. note runner ties into our lab infra so you'll need the credentialized bundle; we'll scrub any internal hostnames.
[05:50] Leo: can we get a quick example of the latency distribution?
[05:52] Diego: sure — median 210ms (bs=1), p95 320ms; bs=8 median 350ms p95 420ms for our sample. bs=16 p95 hit 650ms under burst.
[06:06] Sofia: that p95 420ms at bs=8 is borderline but might be OK. we need to test on our real traffic shape.
[06:12] Maya: agreed. we'll run the shared runner against our staging traffic next week.
[06:18] Lena: next practical suggestion: enable prefix caching on the canary route and set max_batch=8 for interactive route in config. then run the benchmark for 24 hours to get a stable hit rate.
[06:29] Diego: i'll add two more runs: bs=8/16 with cache on/off and send logs. Also try one run with kv=64gb to see hit rate delta.
[06:38] Arjun: ping — what's the expected cost delta if we move to dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted on demand?
[06:43] Lena: preliminary numbers: dedicated reserved reduces per-token infra cost by ~25-35% depending on commit. after cache and batching, net cost may be 40-60% lower than on-demand hosted for steady heavy traffic. we'll show a comparison in the sheet.
[06:58] Maya: timeline question — we need to decide on reserved capacity by end of month.
[07:02] Lena: understood; we'll prioritize the cost spreadsheet updates so you can assess commit sizing.
[07:09] Sofia: any security notes for Private deployment?
[07:11] Samir: short answer — Private supports customer KMS, audit logs, SSO, and can be deployed in VPC or on-prem. we'll share the security pack after this call.
[07:22] Maya: great, next steps?
[07:25] Lena: recap of agreed next steps: Diego runs extra benchmarks (bs=8/16, kv sizes) and shares logs by 9/20; Lena shares updated cost model and assumptions by 9/18; Quantaco confirms target P95 and peak QPS by 9/22; Quantaco to run the runner against staging.
[07:40] Diego: will attach runner script + CSVs.
[07:45] Maya: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll follow up after we run staging tests.

Notes and links referenced: cost spreadsheet link: <redacted>/quantaco-cost-model-2026-09-16.csv, benchmark logs folder: <redacted>/benchmarks/2026-09-16, security pack: <redacted>/redwood-security-pack.pdf

End of transcript.
